questions.q: What is this lesson's actual job, given that every stage in the pipeline was already covered individually?
options: Showing how all eight stages chain together into one working system, rather than teaching any single stage as new material
Introducing a brand-new Fabric item not covered anywhere else in the chapter
Replacing KQL entirely with a no-code alternative
Teaching Databricks Structured Streaming instead of Fabric tools
questions.explain: Every numbered stage is a lesson already built toward — the capstone is the assembly, not new material.

questions.q: In the dashboard's core tile query, which three earlier concepts combine into a single query?
options: Lesson 28's tile mechanism, Lesson 30's tumbling bin(), and Lesson 22's where operator
Lesson 4's Lakehouse, Lesson 10's Fabric Warehouse, and Lesson 12's Direct Lake mode
Lesson 8's Fabric pipelines, Lesson 9's Dataflows Gen2, and Lesson 14's Semantic Models
Lesson 5's Fabric Notebooks, Lesson 6's Shortcuts, and Lesson 7's Copy activity
questions.explain: A rolling 15-minute view of trip volume and average fare, refreshing every minute, is built from exactly those three pieces.

questions.q: Why does the Activator rule in this capstone use a change rule instead of a threshold rule?
options: So it fires once per trip that crosses $200, rather than repeatedly for every re-evaluation while a high fare is still technically current
Change rules are required by KQL syntax for all Activator rules
Threshold rules don't work with FareAmount as a property
There's no real difference between the two rule types in this case
questions.explain: This is Lesson 37's threshold-vs-change distinction, applied to avoid alert spam.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does "done" actually mean for a real-time system?
options: Every layer functioning together — filtering, windowing, deliberate handling of late/out-of-order data, a usable dashboard, and an alert that fires correctly
Simply having data arrive somewhere, regardless of quality or timing
Only having a KQL Database with data in it
Only having an Activator rule configured, regardless of the rest of the pipeline
questions.explain: Missing any one layer doesn't crash the system — it just means something goes quietly wrong somewhere downstream.

questions.q: What happens if a layer like data quality filtering or watermark handling is missing from a real-time pipeline?
options: The system doesn't necessarily crash — something just goes quietly wrong somewhere downstream, unnoticed until it becomes a bigger problem
The entire Eventstream immediately stops running
Fabric automatically detects and fixes the missing layer
Nothing changes at all, since every layer is optional and interchangeable
questions.explain: This is exactly why the chapter built each layer deliberately, rather than treating any of them as optional.
